turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Good afternoon, you're speaking with Daniel from Retailer One. Before we go any further I need to let you know that this call is being recorded for quality assurance and training purposes. Do I have your consent to continue on a recorded line?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Yeah, that's fine, go ahead.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thank you. Can I just confirm I'm speaking with the account holder, Janet Smith, and that you're authorised to make changes to this account?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Yes, that's me. Janet Smith. I'm the account holder, the account's in my name.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Perfect, thank you Janet. And can I confirm the supply address is 12 Ruskin Street, Elwood, Victoria, three one eight four?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: That's the one.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Great. So this is the follow-up on the Saver Flex plan we spoke about last week. Before I take you through any numbers there's a short statement I'm required to read to you in full, so bear with me for a moment.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: No worries.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: The Default Market Offer is the reference price set by the Australian Energy Regulator. The estimated annual cost of this plan is four per cent less than the reference price for an average household in your distribution zone. This is an estimate only, and your actual cost will depend on your usage.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Okay. Four per cent, got it.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thanks for bearing with me. Now, a few things about the plan itself. There's no lock-in contract and no exit fee, so if you find something better in six months you can leave without a penalty from us.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: And there's no connection fee or anything like that?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: No connection fee, that's correct. You're already connected, we're just changing who bills you. The only charges on the plan are your usage and the daily supply charge.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Right. My bill at the moment is around three hundred and forty a quarter.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: That's useful, thank you. Based on that I'd expect you to land somewhere near three hundred and ten a quarter on this plan, but I want to be clear that's an estimate from what you've told me, not a quote. Your real bill depends on what you actually use.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Sure. What happens with the solar?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Good question. The feed-in tariff on Saver Flex is four point five cents for every kilowatt hour you export, and that comes off your bill as a credit each quarter. It's not a cash payment, it offsets what you owe.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Four and a half cents. That's a bit less than what I'm on now.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: It might be, and I'd rather you know that up front than find it on your first bill. Most of the saving on this plan is on the usage side rather than the feed-in side, so whether you come out ahead depends on how much you export versus how much you draw.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Okay, that makes sense. We use most of it during the day anyway.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Then you're in a decent spot. I'll also send you the Basic Plan Information Document which sets all of this out in writing, and you get a ten business day cooling-off period that starts from the day you receive it.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Ten business days from when I get the email?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: That's right, from when you receive it. If you change your mind in that window you call us or reply to the email and we cancel it, no charge, no argument. Nothing moves across until that window has started.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Good. And do I need to do anything with my current retailer?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: No, we handle that. You don't need to ring them or cancel anything. They'll send you a final bill for whatever you've used up to the transfer date, and that's the last you'll hear from them.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: And how long does that take?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Usually it lines up with your next meter read, so anywhere from a couple of weeks to about three months depending on where you sit in the read cycle. I can't give you an exact date today because it's the distributor's schedule, not ours.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Fair enough.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Now a couple of questions I have to ask. Does anyone at the property rely on life support equipment? That's things like a home dialysis machine or an oxygen concentrator.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: No, nothing like that.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thank you. And do you hold a pensioner concession card, health care card or a DVA card? If you do, the concession follows you across and I'd want to make sure it's applied from day one.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: No, no concession card.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Noted, no concession. I'll also mention that if you ever have trouble paying a bill we have a hardship program, and you can call the number on the bill to get on it. I'd rather you know it exists now than find out the hard way.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Appreciate that.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Billing cycle wise, you'll be on quarterly billing to start with, same as you are now. If you'd rather go monthly you can switch that in the app once your account's live, it takes about thirty seconds.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Quarterly's fine for now.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: No problem. Is the meter accessible? Some of the older Elwood places have the box inside a locked side gate and the meter reader can't get in, which means you end up on estimated reads.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: It's on the front wall, no gate. They can get to it.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: That's the easy version, good. Is it a smart meter or an older accumulation meter? If it's a smart meter you'll get your usage in the app daily, which most people find useful.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: It was replaced a few years ago, so I think it's a smart one. It's got a digital display.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: That'll be a smart meter then. I'll confirm it against the distributor record before anything goes through, but that won't change the plan or the pricing either way.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Okay. And can I still get paper bills? My husband likes them on paper.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: You can. There's a small fee for paper billing on some plans but not on this one, it's included. You'll get the email copy as well so you've got both.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: That works.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: And are you planning to move in the next twelve months at all? It doesn't stop anything, it just means I'd flag the account so the transfer team knows to expect it.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: No, we're staying put.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Good. Last of the housekeeping. Is there anyone else who should be on the account with you, a joint account holder? You can add someone later but it's easier now.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Just me for now.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Just you, noted. Right, that's the admin out of the way. Let me pull the pricing up on my screen and I'll take you through the actual numbers so you can see what you're agreeing to.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Yep, that's the bit I want to hear.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: One second, it's just loading. Some of these older screens take their time, sorry about that.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: All good, take your time.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Here we go. So before I read the rates, just so you know how to read them, everything I'm about to quote you is GST inclusive. Some retailers quote you the ex-GST number and it looks cheaper than it is.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: That's annoying. Yes, including is fine.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Agreed. And this is a single rate tariff, so there's no peak and off-peak split to worry about. One usage rate, all day, plus the daily supply charge.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Simpler. My current one has three different rates and I've never understood it.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: So what's the rate?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Right, here are the numbers. On the Saver Flex plan your peak usage rate is 28.6 cents per kilowatt hour including GST, and the daily supply charge is 98.45 cents a day.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Twenty-eight point six. And what am I on now?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: From the bill you sent through you're on thirty-three point one cents, so that's a reasonable step down on usage. The supply charge is within a cent or two of what you're paying now.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: That's better than I expected, actually.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: It's a competitive plan at the moment. The one thing I'll say, and I say it to everyone, is that the usage rate isn't locked. We can change it with notice. You'd get written notice before any change and you can leave at that point with no exit fee.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: How much notice?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Minimum five business days before it takes effect, and it comes by email or post, whichever you've chosen. In practice most changes land at the start of July with the regulated price reset.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Right, so July is the one to watch.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: That's the one. And there's no discount that expires on this plan either, which is the other thing that catches people. The rate I've quoted you is just the rate, there's no conditional discount that drops off after twelve months.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: That's what happened with the last mob. Great for a year then it doubled.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: It's a common story. Nothing on this plan behaves like that. So, that's the pricing. Are you happy for me to go ahead and set this up?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Yes, let's do it.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thank you Janet. I'll take that as your consent to transfer the electricity account at 12 Ruskin Street to Retailer One on the Saver Flex plan on the terms I've just been through. Is that correct?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Yes, that's correct.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Wonderful. Let me just get this into the system. Bear with me one moment.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Sure.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Sorry about that, the form timed out on me and I had to start it again. Thanks for waiting.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: No problem, I thought you'd hung up on me.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Still here, apologies. Right, payment. Would you like to set up direct debit, or would you rather pay each bill manually when it arrives?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Direct debit's easier. Off the card, not the bank account.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Card is fine. Just so you know, direct debit comes out three business days after the bill date, and you'll get the bill by email before it's taken so there are no surprises.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Fine. Do you want the card number now?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Please, whenever you're ready. Take it slowly for me.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: It's 4511 2233 4455 6677, expiry zero eight twenty nine, and the three on the back are 419.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Got that, thank you. That's gone straight into the payment gateway, I don't see the full number on my side. Nothing will be charged today, the first debit is three days after your first bill.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Good.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Almost done. What's the best email address for your welcome pack and your contract? This is the one the cooling-off notice goes to as well, so it matters that I get it right.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Let me think, I use a couple.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Whichever one you check most.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Use j dot smith at gmail dot com. That's j for Janet, dot, s-m-i-t-h, at gmail dot com.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Lovely, got it, thank you.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: And just to confirm the NMI off your bill, I've got 6 1 0 2 0 3 4 5 6 7 8. Does that match the number on the front page of your last bill?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Hang on. Six one zero two zero three four five six seven eight. Yes, that matches.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Perfect. And this is electricity only, isn't it? You're not looking to bring gas across at this stage?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Electricity only. We're all electric here, no gas connected.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Electricity only, noted. So that's everything. You'll get the welcome pack and the Basic Plan Information Document by email within one business day, your cooling-off period runs ten business days from when that lands, and there's nothing else you need to do.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: And if the email doesn't turn up?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Check your junk folder first, then call the number on our website and we'll resend it. Thanks very much for your time today Janet, you have a good afternoon.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: You too. Thanks Daniel. Bye.
